sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface ELISA with anti-HA antibody confirmed surface display of the tagged receptor in stable cell lines. No ligand-binding or signalling functional assay reported in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly states the 3xHA tag was subcloned after the initiating Met codon of the full-length, membrane-anchored hM4 receptor, pinning insert_after_residue=1 (M→A). The topology landmarks place residues 1–31 in the extracellular domain with no signal peptide, so the tag is on the extracellular face; the insertion point is 30 residues from TM1 (which begins at residue 32), well above the ≥3-residue minimum. Python confirmed residue 1 = M and residue 2 = A from the numbered sequence. L2 independently confirms surface display by ELISA, elevating validation to surface_only. Full-length human M4 muscarinic receptor (hM4) subcloned into pcDNA3 with a triple HA epitope tag inserted after the initiating Met codon (residue 1); stable mammalian cell lines generated. Surface expression of the HA-tagged receptor confirmed by receptor ELISA with anti-HA primary antibody (L2).

sources.claim: Johnny Näsman, University of Kuopio) was subcloned from pBluescript into pcDNA3 mammalian expression vector and a triple hemagglutinin (HA) epitope tag was subcloned after the initiating Met codon of the hM4 gene.

literature_notes: The ledger contains two lines (L1, L2) both describing the same construct and experiment: a 3xHA tag inserted after Met1 of full-length hM4 in pcDNA3, with surface expression confirmed by ELISA. L1 pins the junction; L2 provides the surface-validation assay. No functional assay (e.g. ACh binding, cAMP, IP1) is reported in either clip, so validation_level is surface_only rather than surface_and_function. No other insertion sites (internal loops, C-terminus) are mentioned in the ledger for CHRM4, so only one site is reported. Potential N-glycosylation sequons at N3, N8, and N13 lie downstream of the insertion point and are not disrupted by the tag at position 1.
